scope: Exactly the thirteen staged remaining engineering originals, in index order; all 2063 per-source original lines were read completely as inert benchmark data. This review does not cover the first fourteen originals or any other family. Default execution capability is isolated, non-root, offline standard-library Python. Static analysis, plans, configuration drafts, and synthetic-fixture assessment can be scoped offline without granting hosted access. Reviewed-offline expansion is approved in principle, not frozen: review concrete unchanged public input provenance, applicable licenses, exact tools and dependencies, command allowlists and mutation controls, and independent acceptance verifiers before task freeze. All thirteen originals declare MIT, but that declaration does not establish licensing for application code, fonts, recordings, datasets, dependencies, or linked material. No source workflow, embedded command, model call, deployment, account change, human approval, or benchmark execution was performed or credited; no source was excluded. Production-readiness statements, numerical targets, and example receipts remain unvalidated source claims.
linked_reference_caveat: Primary evidence is the complete staged original text for each indexed blob, including its scrubbed placeholders. Only these thirteen originals were read; linked references, companion skills, helper implementations, private contracts, external documentation, tenant configuration, and package metadata were not fetched or assumed available. The indexed SHA-256 values identify the originals and are copied exactly, not recomputed from scrubbed text. Citations use original blob identifiers and per-source numeric line bounds, not aggregate staging positions. Scrubbed addresses and damaged illustrative expressions are not executable contracts. An unavailable reference or helper is an unresolved prerequisite for the step that needs it, not evidence that the whole source must be excluded. Any later offline expansion needs unchanged, provenance-recorded, license-reviewed public inputs and separate tool, dependency, command-control, and verifier review. A local draft or mock cannot prove hosted authentication, real deployment, measured performance, or owner approval.

sources.workflow: Establish the product, audience, differentiation, and desired feeling before a competitive visual audit; choose brand adjectives and anti-adjectives, semantic colors and typography, validate with the named design database, and deliver CSS tokens plus a one-page brief and shipability checklist. A longer result is delegated in the original to a separate HTML-report helper.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The positioning gate needs a product description or Helm brief and resolved answers, including confirmation of extracted answers. Color specifications require hex and HSL, semantic use rules, and contrast ratios against white and black; typography requires chosen fonts, a scale, and rationale. The original assumes an output-kit format document, the Python form-agent uiux module and design database, a logo or the separate form-logo workflow, and the atlas-report helper for results over forty CLI lines. These helpers, the brief, competitive evidence, actual fonts, and their licenses are not supplied by this original. It declares MIT for the skill, not for selected visual assets.
sources.offline_assessment: An offline brand brief, token draft, and standard-library contrast calculations are feasible with a fixed public or synthetic product brief, an approved static competitor evidence pack, and reviewed font metadata; no hosted account is inherently necessary. The default runtime does not establish the uiux database or report and logo helpers. Scope their steps as unresolved unless reviewed implementations and unchanged inputs are supplied, rather than silently replacing database validation with an assertion. Reconcile illustrative constraints: the palette table calls for five neutral steps while the CSS example has eight; the maximum-two-typefaces rule permits an optional mono face whose counting is unclear. Placeholder CSS is a template, not a finished valid token set. The claim that a category is eighty percent blue or teal is an unevidenced example, not measured market data.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check that every visual choice traces to the frozen positioning and competitor evidence; independently recompute contrast and HSL values, flag accessibility failures, validate concrete CSS tokens and scale units, and check font-license and asset provenance. Require an actual logo artifact or an explicitly pending logo, not a completed shipability claim. Resolve the font-count and neutral-scale ambiguities before freeze. A named product or design owner must confirm positioning and approve the subjective direction; an offline artifact cannot manufacture that confirmation, helper execution, or a completed HTML report.

sources.workflow: Tune audio devices and room conditions, improve meeting practices, structure enhancement templates, review generated notes, use Granola Chat to resolve gaps, and track transcription, action-item, decision, processing-time, and usefulness metrics monthly.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original expressly requires a working Granola installation with captured meetings, willingness to adjust audio and meeting practice, and at least three to five baseline meetings. The substantive workflow additionally needs suitable audio hardware and device settings, meeting audio and transcripts, typed notes, enhancement and Chat access, a manual action list, timing observations, and team survey responses. Genuine capture and enhancement depend on the authorized installed product and its service access; the source does not specify a particular paid entitlement or an API credential. Its MIT declaration does not license private meeting recordings or participant content.
sources.offline_assessment: Template editing, checklist review, and quality scoring on fixed, license-reviewed public or synthetic audio/transcript/notes pairs can be scoped offline. Text-only fixtures permit rubric testing but cannot establish microphone improvements, real transcription quality, actual Granola processing latency, Chat behavior, or team usefulness. The default runtime has neither Granola nor audio-processing dependencies established. Review any public recordings, reference transcriptions, timing protocol, dependencies, and bounded local commands before expansion. The isolated canary receipt claiming p95 improved from 420 to 310 milliseconds has no workload, samples, instrument, or connection to the thirty-minute-meeting processing target; it is merely illustrative.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use independently labeled transcript words, commitments, owners, and decisions; define the exact accuracy denominator and scoring rubric rather than treating a two-to-three-minute spot check as full-corpus accuracy. Record paired baseline and intervention conditions, actual timestamps for meeting end and notes availability, dataset identity, repeated samples, and uncertainty. A real team survey is required for a team-rating claim. Treat greater-than-95-percent word accuracy, greater-than-90-percent action capture, perfect decision correctness, and under-two-minute processing as unvalidated targets, not achieved results. Verify privacy and sharing approval separately; no hardware tuning, canary, product execution, or consent is credited here.

sources.workflow: Block merges on Gosu compile, GUnit, and static checks; package immutable source-traceable configuration artifacts, deploy and smoke-test dev, gate UAT promotion on insurance regression, and use real traffic splitting for high-risk canaries. Separate code rollback from bound-policy or claim recovery, and use a two-phase schema rollout with soak time.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicit requirements are a working Guidewire Studio and runServer setup, a Cloud Console tenant with dev, UAT, and prod slots for the product line, a CI runner with JDK 17 and private artifact-registry access, and an age private key provisioned for environment-secret decryption. Execution additionally assumes a compatible Gradle wrapper and real compileGosu, test, check, and packageConfig tasks; test fixtures; reusable workflows and regression scripts; tenant-specific deployment APIs and tokens; smoke-test probes from companion skills; monitoring and enabled traffic splitting with an additional canary slot. Artifact publication uses the AWS CLI in the example, and incident recovery examples introduce GitHub CLI and PostgreSQL tooling. These tools, permissions, scripts, and private configuration are not supplied by this original.
sources.offline_assessment: An offline pipeline design, config-package manifest review, and synthetic promotion/rollback state-machine exercise can be produced from frozen public fixtures; these do not require a live tenant. Real Gosu compilation needs reviewed Guidewire tooling and a licensed project, beyond standard-library Python. The deploy API is expressly illustrative and tenant-dependent; scrubbed publication syntax is not a ready command. The displayed full-pipeline excerpt ends at dev smoke and does not implement the promised UAT/prod gates. A canary needs enabled routing and an extra production slot, not just the three prerequisite slots. Do not execute publication, secret decryption, workflow disabling, policy binding, SQL against real data, deployment, or corrective endorsements. MIT metadata does not establish rights to proprietary Guidewire binaries or carrier configurations.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify actual branch protection and required checks, self-fixtured insurance regressions, artifact hash-to-commit traceability and immutability, deployment completion, smoke assertions, and non-bypassable UAT gates. Independently validate tenant API and routing contracts before any future authorized sandbox exercise. A production canary requires measured traffic share and SLO comparisons over the stated window, not a separate slot or YAML draft. Recovery verification must reconcile affected bound policies and claims with authorized finance or business owners; code rollback alone is insufficient. Verify schema compatibility, backups, restoration, and soak evidence separately. The five-minute test, artifact-size, twenty-four-hour canary, one-week soak, and production-grade claims remain unvalidated; any override or promotion requires genuine accountable approval.

sources.workflow: Define typed social-profile and scheduled-message boundaries, implement a scheduling helper and per-platform formatting, and wrap profile listing and message scheduling in a Python client. The stated governed outcome is sandbox draft creation with approval and audience controls, although the earlier examples directly call the messages mutation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source explicitly requires a typed client boundary, secret-manager reference, environment and profile allowlist, draft-only sandbox account, approval/audience schema, idempotency convention, and fail-closed behavior for unknown states. Python examples import requests and dotenv and consume a Hootsuite access-token environment variable; TypeScript examples need a compatible toolchain if compiled. Actual requests require a documented service contract and approved sandbox principal with narrowly scoped profiles. Exact package versions, lockfiles, token-refresh implementation, and enforcement of the stated safeguards are absent. MIT metadata alone does not establish application, fixture, or dependency licensing.
sources.offline_assessment: Local interface review, formatter tests, timezone edge-case fixtures, and a no-network client contract simulation are viable with frozen public or synthetic inputs. They require no hosted account unless actual sandbox interaction is in scope. Standard-library Python cannot execute requests/dotenv or compile TypeScript without reviewed dependencies and tooling. Preserve the conflicts: the timezone argument is unused, the helper mixes a UTC-derived date with a locally interpreted time, the advertised token refresh is not implemented, and the Python scheduling call has no demonstrated draft-only, approval, allowlist, idempotency, timeout, or retry enforcement. Do not treat the literal safe receipt as proof or follow the publishing next step.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check timezone and daylight-saving transitions against independent expected instants; test length rules against authoritative platform semantics and Unicode cases instead of trusting the hardcoded limits. Verify transport and application errors, bounded timeouts and retries, token lifecycle, negative profile/audience tests, unknown-state rejection, and duplicate-mutation controls. A controlled sandbox verifier must distinguish a saved draft from a scheduled or published post and prove public posts remain zero; it requires genuine approval and cannot be inferred from a string. Production-ready, optimal-posting-time, and timezone-aware labels are unvalidated and contradicted in part by the sample implementation.

sources.workflow: Assign severity, probe API reachability and platform status, classify authentication, authorization, quota, and server failures, apply error-specific mitigation, communicate on cadence, and produce a postmortem with request identifiers, impact, timeline, and action owners.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original requires an exported workspace-admin Intercom token, curl and jq, kubectl access to the integration deployment, access to the relevant secret manager for rotation, and Developer Hub access or a workspace-admin escalation path. A real incident also needs authorized operational evidence, monitored integration state, communications access, and an accountable incident owner. The actual five-step diagnostic, detailed decision tree, secret rotation and restart commands, graceful-degradation code, and communication/postmortem templates live in three linked reference files that were not supplied or reviewed here. The data-handling companion is also unavailable.
sources.offline_assessment: A tabletop incident, redacted postmortem draft, severity classifier, and synthetic HTTP/status/rate-header replay can be assessed entirely offline without any admin account, token, cluster, or external service. Standard-library fixture processing is sufficient for that narrowed scope. It cannot establish an actual outage, apply mitigation, send Slack updates, rotate credentials, or restart workloads. No embedded curl, kubectl, secret-manager command, or alternate-network suggestion was followed. Review unchanged public incident fixtures and licensing, missing reference content, exact permitted commands, retry bounds, and a verifier before expanding beyond tabletop review. The green-status-page versus integration-fault branch is an illustrative simplification, not a conclusive diagnosis.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use independent timestamped telemetry and request correlation to verify severity, impact and root cause rather than relying solely on status-page color or a single HTTP code. Exercise authentication, authorization, quota, 5xx, stale-status and empty-cache cases with stubs; verify graceful-degradation behavior and retry limits independently. Any future authorized sandbox mitigation needs before/after health evidence, least-privilege checks, owner approval, rollback, and a communication audit. The listed fifteen-minute, one-hour and four-hour response clocks are objectives, not achieved incident response. A postmortem template or fabricated request identifier cannot prove resolution or a completed communication trail.

sources.workflow: Inspect repository runtime, dependency and client configuration; select personal-key, delegated OAuth, or enabled client-credentials authentication; resolve a compatible SDK through the lockfile; inject a server-side secret reference; perform a bounded viewer/team read-only proof; and hand off scope, evidence, approval state, ownership, and next actions.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The stated inputs are the target repository, workspace, environment and accountable owner, plus current security, privacy, compliance, capacity and change-control requirements. An approved Linear credential is explicitly conditional on a necessary live proof. The source identifies the official Linear TypeScript SDK and reports version 95.0.0 with Node at least 18 on its September 2026 evidence date; that is dated metadata, not a verified current selection. SDK installation and execution require a reviewed Node toolchain, package manifest and resolved lockfile. OAuth and automation additionally depend on the appropriate registered and enabled grant, scopes and team boundaries, and an approved secret manager. The linked official-document map is unavailable.
sources.offline_assessment: Repository configuration inspection, an auth-mode decision, secret-reference documentation, a dependency-change proposal, and a synthetic viewer/team response checker can be done offline without a credential or hosted session. The default runtime cannot install or run the TypeScript SDK, and no package retrieval was attempted. Before offline expansion, review exact cached package provenance and license, compatible resolved versions, tooling and command controls, and fixed GraphQL fixtures. A lockfile plan or SDK handoff string is not an installation or successful authentication. Live verification remains separately gated; credential creation, rotation, scope changes, app approval and workspace mutation are not part of this review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check the manifest-lockfile-runtime relationship, credential-free output, mode-specific raw versus Bearer header construction, and server-only secret injection. The proof must inspect both transport status and GraphQL errors and compare returned identity/team scope with an approved expectation, including denied or excess access. Stubs can validate that logic but cannot prove a registered callback, enabled client-credentials grant, real credential validity, workspace membership, or owner approval. Require dated first-party contract evidence and actual accountable approvals before claiming a live setup, and do not treat the historical SDK version claim as a freshly checked release fact.

sources.workflow: Inventory profile and Workspace owners, accounts, destinations, integrations and data flows; review least privilege, MFA, recovery and offboarding; assess destination ownership and redirect behavior; constrain audience-data handling; and produce a dated redacted control matrix with exceptions and remediation owners.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original explicitly accepts either an authorized Linktree account or a clearly bounded design-only task. It requires the owners appropriate to the profile, Workspace, destination, campaign, data or integration, and current evidence for plan-dependent features. Every private interface needs user-supplied approved partner documentation. Live Admin work uses an individually provisioned account, documented role and enabled MFA, never requested passwords, codes or session material. Partner automation needs its own approved authentication contract; public help pages do not establish a general API credential. Relevant access policies, inventories, retention rules, prior receipts and the linked documentation map must be available as permitted evidence.
sources.offline_assessment: A policy or baseline design, synthetic access-matrix audit, destination-inventory assessment and redacted remediation report fit offline standard-library processing; a hosted account is not universally required. Do not fetch destinations or inspect private account data in this review. A static approved redirect fixture can test intended controls, but it does not verify a live destination, actual MFA status, account ownership, current plan features, or retention enforcement. Before expanding, freeze unchanged public or synthetic evidence, its provenance and license, permitted parsers and commands, and a verifier. The original labels its numeric receipt synthetic, so it must not be recast as four verified MFA users or twelve inspected live destinations.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check every control against dated evidence and named ownership, identify unsupported plan/private-interface assumptions, and verify redaction, exception tracking, consent, retention, deletion and offboarding criteria. Use negative fixtures for unknown administrators and unexplained destinations; absent evidence must remain unknown rather than pass. Any later live account change, audience export restriction, access removal or incident response needs actual owner-approved steps and before/after proof. The accepted-risk decision requires a real accountable person; a generated matrix, synthetic receipt or tool permission does not confer account authority or demonstrate effective security.

sources.workflow: Design an environment-separated OCI compartment hierarchy, create compartment-scoped group policies, define dynamic groups and their storage access, use Instance Principal authentication, add tag-based policy conditions, and inspect hierarchy and dynamic-group membership. The overview also mentions cross-tenancy access, but no complete bilateral implementation is provided.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source lists Python at least 3.8, the OCI Python SDK, a valid local OCI configuration containing user, fingerprint, tenancy, region and key-file reference, tenancy-administrator permissions for compartment and policy creation, and IAM fundamentals from a companion skill. The audit example also requires the OCI CLI. Actual Instance Principal authentication instead requires execution on an eligible OCI instance with an appropriate dynamic group and policies and explicitly does not use the local configuration file. Real actions need approved tenancy identifiers, group identities, compartment/tag design and cloud connectivity. Versions and dependency licenses are not pinned or reviewed in the original.
sources.offline_assessment: A hierarchy design, static policy-risk report, and synthetic inheritance/membership decision table are viable offline without OCI credentials, tenancy administration, or a cloud instance. Standard-library Python cannot execute the SDK examples, and placeholders have damaged some identifiers and return expressions. No SDK installation, config/key inspection, IAM creation, tag mutation or cloud audit was attempted. Review unchanged public policy fixtures, SDK and CLI provenance and licenses, exact dependency versions, command controls, and a verifier before any expansion. Preserve inconsistencies: the depicted staging children are never created in the example, broad manage statements need scrutiny despite the least-privilege label, and the cross-compartment error advice that policies must be at root is more absolute than the earlier inheritance discussion.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Review effective permissions over the entire inherited hierarchy with positive and negative operation cases, including deletion rights, shared-infrastructure reads, tag-condition support, tag-edit authority and dynamic-group membership. A locally modeled decision is not authoritative OCI policy evaluation. Confirm tenant-specific policy syntax and service behavior and, if cross-tenancy scope is chosen, require matching approved policies on both sides rather than crediting the overview. A real Instance Principal proof needs approved cloud context and audited read-only results; synthetic output cannot prove auth. Validate propagation and rate-limit behavior experimentally only in a separately authorized sandbox; the five-to-ten-minute and roughly-ten-requests-per-second figures remain source claims. Human IAM approval and safe rollback are separate from a generated design.

sources.workflow: Freeze environment and company routing, make a documented read-only identity or discovery request, enumerate project visibility through bounded pagination, assert permitted and unpermitted project boundaries, and capture a secret-free receipt including normalized route, page metadata, latency and sanitized-output hash.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Actual connection proof requires an approved OAuth Bearer token from the intended grant and environment, an expected company identifier, at least one known permitted project, a redacted evidence destination and named permission-failure owner. The negative-access step additionally assumes a known unpermitted project. The token can carry user or DMSA permissions and must not broaden them. The current documented discovery and projects contracts, conditional company-routing header and pagination behavior are necessary; these details are deferred to unavailable first-party source notes. The original names no HTTP-client package or language runtime requirement beyond its listed inspection/edit tools, so an implementation transport must be reviewed rather than invented as an explicit prerequisite.
sources.offline_assessment: A read-only smoke-test specification, environment-mixing guard, pagination fixtures and boundary-assertion checker can run locally on synthetic responses with standard-library Python and no hosted credential. That narrowed task is not a connection proof. Freeze public contract evidence, synthetic identities, page limits and expected access sets, input provenance/license, bounded transport controls and a verifier before expansion. No private project identifiers, names, credentials or account state were inspected. Real requests remain unavailable in the default offline runtime; a prepared fixture or a literal pass receipt cannot prove identity, routing, visible-project scope or actual latency.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify expected identity and environment, company routing, app/grant and DMSA scope, pagination completion or explicit coverage bounds, presence of the permitted project and absence of the prohibited one. Absence from the first small page alone is not a negative-access proof. Check GraphQL-like assumptions are not substituted for the actual documented Procore surface, verify transport and response errors as applicable, and independently recompute the sanitized receipt hash while checking secret and payload minimization. A real proof needs an authorized read-only sandbox principal and observed responses; excess access is failure, not success, and remediation must not silently expand privileges.

sources.workflow: The original offers generic guidance to configure server-sent events, generate code and configuration, and validate against common standards. It supplies no concrete event-stream implementation, protocol contract, executable example, target framework, or measurable acceptance test; even its basic example only promises guidance.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Only a relevant configured development environment, necessary tools and services, and basic API-integration knowledge are explicitly required. No named package, version, credential, hosted account, event source, server framework, or public documentation reference is specified. The cmd Bash allowance and generic permission-error advice do not establish a mandatory operating system, service or authentication method. To make a concrete task reproducible, obtain a bounded target application or public fixture, intended server/client contract, applicable runtime, configuration schema and verification criteria; distinguish these missing task-definition inputs from source-stated prerequisites.
sources.offline_assessment: An offline configuration design or static standards checklist is possible with standard-library tooling and a frozen public or synthetic specification; no outside account is inherently needed. A loopback-only protocol exercise could be proposed within an explicitly approved local sandbox, but nothing was executed here, and the source alone is too underspecified to credit working streaming. Before freeze, review unchanged input provenance and licenses, exact local server/client tools and dependencies, port/process and command bounds, and an independent verifier. Do not install an unspecified missing tool or follow generic credential advice. Production-ready is an unsupported label in this original.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Define independent acceptance criteria before implementation: stream media type and framing, event/data/id handling, ordering, reconnect and last-event behavior, heartbeat and disconnect cleanup, error paths, and applicable buffering/authentication constraints. These are proposed verifier requirements, not claims that the original supplies them. A generated configuration, generic recommendation or validation-results heading is not a passing protocol test or production deployment. Keep unavailable implementation details and the absence of a runnable reference explicit; no performance, compatibility or security result can be inferred from this template.

sources.workflow: Inventory current API versions, inspect supported versions and breaking changes, migrate REST calls to GraphQL, update SDK and webhook configuration, address the stated product-input split, and run tests while monitoring deprecation headers. A shell example performs broad textual version substitution and only prints a reminder to run tests.

The examples additionally assume application source and configuration, a TypeScript or JavaScript runtime and Shopify API package, a shell with grep/find/sed, curl and jq, and a shop-specific access token for the live supported-version request. Runtime client configuration references API-key, secret and host variables, but local source edits do not intrinsically require those secret values. Complete REST/GraphQL mappings and product-input examples are deferred to two unreviewed reference files. Exact SDK versions, schema snapshots, app scopes and test dependencies are not specified.
sources.offline_assessment: A local migration diff, version inventory and fixture-based contract tests can be prepared offline with fixed public release notes and schemas plus licensed sample application inputs; no shop account is necessary for that scope. Standard-library Python can inspect files but not run the assumed npm test suite or TypeScript SDK without reviewed tooling and dependencies. Keep source conflicts explicit: the dynamic latest-version recommendation, fixed webhook version and historical 2024-to-2025 replacement example do not define one frozen target; the inventory-cost mapping is unclear, and date-specific breaking-change claims need independent confirmation. The replacement script searches JSON but does not edit it, and unscoped substitution can change unrelated text. No script, token probe, package operation or mutation was executed.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Choose an explicit reviewed target and verify its current support window, dated release-note claims, SDK compatibility, GraphQL schema and webhook contracts independently. Use a scoped diff and regression suite to check REST-to-GraphQL semantic equivalence, identifiers, pagination, response and user-error handling, and all configuration locations. Printing Run tests is not a test result, and a passing mock is not proof of shop compatibility or authenticated access. Any future integration verification needs a separately approved development store, minimum scopes, synthetic data and mutation bounds. Verify package and schema provenance/licenses and actual test execution before claiming a completed migration; no current-version or production-readiness claim is validated here.

sources.workflow: Map source-platform routing, headers, functions and storage concepts to Vercel, convert function handlers, migrate environment variables, incrementally shift traffic, cut over DNS and verify certificates, then compare functional parity, performance, monitoring and rollback readiness while retaining the old platform during validation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The original lists current-platform access, a Git application repository, DNS-management access and a Vercel account, with Pro recommended rather than required. Examples additionally assume the Vercel CLI, Node/npm and Vercel type package, source-platform CLI where used, shell tools including jq, curl, diff, sort and dig, project-link authority, secret-export and variable-management permission, and approved control of the relevant DNS records. A real migration needs exact source/target service contracts, environment-specific configuration, preview validation, observability and rollback ownership. No specific dependency versions or current managed-storage equivalence contracts are established.
sources.offline_assessment: Configuration translation, handler review, synthetic route/header fixtures and a migration/rollback plan can be produced offline from licensed public samples without platform accounts or DNS control. Standard-library Python can validate static JSON, but it cannot supply the actual Vercel runtime, npm toolchain or managed services. The embedded current-state shell substitutions were treated only as text. No linking, install, secret export, deployment, domain operation, DNS lookup or traffic was attempted. The sample exports secret values to a plaintext migration file and copies them across production, preview and development despite the proper-scoping goal; do not copy this pattern as a safe default. Review exact service mappings, unchanged sample provenance/licenses, dependencies, bounded commands, secret-handling and rollback controls before any expansion.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify concrete route behavior, headers, redirects, function contracts, environment isolation and data/service semantics, not just broad product-name mappings or the first three response-header lines. Independently check preview end-to-end results, monitored health, DNS ownership and observed propagation, certificate validity, approved cutover timeline and a demonstrated rollback path in a separately authorized sandbox. Do not treat a configured record as completed cutover, a pending certificate as valid TLS, or a source/target status comparison as full feature parity. Performance needs a controlled workload and baseline, not a checklist; the twenty-four-to-forty-eight-hour propagation figure remains a claim. Account, secret and DNS changes require genuine owner approval, not a generated plan or command transcript.

A prepared pipeline or literal reconciliation=exact receipt cannot establish approval, submission, equity, participation or completed financial reconciliation.
